title: Sunny and the Big Old Gum Tree
description: Little Sonny the quokka visits the oldest, grandest tree in the bush and feels its quiet, peaceful wisdom. A calm, gentle bedtime story for little ones. Part of Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
At the very edge of the clearing, there was a tree that was much older and much taller than all the others.

Its trunk was so wide that Sunny couldn't wrap his arms even halfway around it. Its bark was thick and wrinkled and peeling in long strips, revealing smooth pale patches underneath. Its branches spread out high above everything, like enormous arms stretched wide and easy.

This was the Big Old Gum Tree.

Sunny came here sometimes when he wanted to think.

Today, he walked up to the tree slowly, placed both his small paws flat against the rough warm bark, and pressed his cheek against it.

The tree was warm from the afternoon sun. It smelled of eucalyptus, dry and clean and green.

Sunny stayed very still.

He could feel something — something he couldn't quite name. A stillness. A patience. The tree had been here for a very, very long time, through many storms and dry summers and cold nights and bright mornings. And it was still here. Still growing. Still reaching upwards.

Above Sunny, a koala was curled high in the branches, sleeping its long koala sleep. A family of tiny birds darted in and out of a hollow. The leaves rustled very softly in a breeze Sunny couldn't even feel from down below.

He sat down at the base of the tree, his back against the warm trunk, his face turned up to look at all those high green leaves.

The evening light came slowly, turning the leaves to gold.

Sunny felt very calm. Very held. Very small in the nicest possible way.

He closed his eyes, and listened to the tree breathe.

Goodnight, little Sunny. Goodnight, big old gum tree. Goodnight, ancient and patient and good.
